herbal_anatomical_extent.observed: One continuous root-crown and multiple upward stalks with two large deeply divided basal blades, smaller serrated/lobed leaves, several blue-edged oval heads and a conspicuous blue terminal flower. Thick brown crown divides into numerous curved/tapered arms including a conspicuous lower crossing/open-loop geometry.
herbal_anatomical_extent.limits: Anatomical terms describe drawn geometry; no species identity, naturalistic accuracy, botanical family or counted real organ is inferred.

fragment_anatomical_extent.contrast_if_second_object_is_target: Securely narrower drawn extent than full herbal plant: no attached leaves or flower are shown for this separate shape.
fragment_anatomical_extent.qualification_limit: This conditional extent difference cannot establish the fragment240 relation until catalogue/native owner mapping is resolved.

distinctive_concordance.literal_second_object: Both have bulky root bodies and curved/tapering arms, but this is generic root-like resemblance. No stable distinctive branching/open-loop homology was secured.
distinctive_concordance.rival_object3: Deep marginal green-blade division supplies possible leaf resemblance; this remains a separate possible owner.
distinctive_concordance.rival_object4: Multiple brown tapering root arms supply a generic root counterpart; no same topology is established.

counter_features: Herbal root has one elongated neck feeding a broad central crown with many longer curved arms fanning to both sides and downward; visible object2 is a compact red-brown lateral mass with short blunt crown stubs and much of its tapered mass directed right.
Herbal lower roots include conspicuous crossing/open-loop arms; object2 has a different lower open curve, without a secure corresponding branch topology.

Large divided basal leaves and blue flower/head architecture of the herbal are absent from visible object2. Their absence supports a partial-extent hypothesis only after coidentity is established, not identity by itself.
Visual object3 has a different broad-base/long taper root; visual object4 has a different narrow parallel-root fan and oval leaf architecture. They are retained rivals.
Red versus ochre/brown paint is recorded but not treated as a diagnostic taxonomic exclusion.
